ashby:skydio:67a8f6ab-a581-426f-8047-968.summary: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders , soldiers in battlefield scenarios , and beyond .

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: Skydio is seeking an experienced operations leader to join our team as Senior Manager, Solutions Engineering for Launch Team Readiness, West. This role leads the readiness function for the weastern half of the dock business, owning the customer journey from pre-sales readiness — technical, policy, and operational — through deployment, training, and go-live, and it is measured on the team's outcomes rather than your own: on-time deployments, smooth launches, and confident customers.

This is a remote role. Travel of 50 to 60% is required to support customer engagements, field activities, deployments, team onsites, and company events, with heavier travel expected during periods of team growth and onboarding.
This role reports to the Director, Launch Team.

sections.title: About the Team:
paras: The Launch Team is the operational arm of Skydio's dock business. We sit between the opportunity and the running program, and readiness means everything an agency needs to launch: the site, the policy and public approval behind it, the flight operation that will run it, and a clean handoff to Customer Success. We do not perform every piece of that work, but we project manage the customer to all of it and are accountable for the date.

The team is measured on time-to-launch, readiness gate adherence, deployment schedule performance, and the condition of the program at handoff. Readiness capacity is sized against dock site volume, so the function has to scale faster than headcount.

Readiness Specialists are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Solutions Engineers, Deployment Engineering, Legal and Policy, and Customer Success to support successful deployments and the long-term success of Public Safety sUAS programs

sections.title: Lead the team
bullets: Hire, onboard, coach, and retain your team of Readiness Specialists, with clear ownership and coverage across the accounts in your region, and develop people beyond the seat they are in.
Set the bar for readiness quality — site readiness standards, launch checklists, training delivery, and handoff documentation that hold up in front of a chief, a sheriff, or a city council.
Own capacity and account assignment across your region, balancing launch complexity against specialist experience, and make the tradeoffs visible to leadership.

sections.title: Drive on-time launches
bullets: Own the health of the readiness portfolio across the West region, with visibility into site readiness, policy and approval milestones, deployment and training progress, and launch criteria on every active account.
Identify at-risk launches early and drive resolution, escalating when blockers exceed the team's authority, and directly own complex, strategic, or recovering launches when the situation warrants.
Work closely with your counterpart in the East so the two halves of the readiness function run one motion rather than two.
Partner with Sales and Solutions Engineering leadership to align readiness capacity with pipeline, and advise on site feasibility and launch requirements for strategic pursuits.

ashby:skydio:d5b1ab09-41cb-4f50-9ac8-683.summary: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders , soldiers in battlefield scenarios , and beyond .

sections.title: About the Team:
paras: The Customer Success team helps customers turn Skydio into a reliable, repeatable, and enduring operating advantage. We are a rapidly growing team of passionate, mission-driven professionals, who sweat the details and ensure our customers are set up for success.

sections.title: About the role:
paras: We are looking for a motivated Customer Success Manager with a deep sense of ownership to lead and drive all aspects of implementation, usage and adoption, retention and expansion of our Canadian public sector and commercial customers. ashby:snowflake:b071b406-6bd0-4def-ba95-.summary: At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

sections.title: ABOUT THE ROLE
paras: Streamlit has become a defining force in the Python ecosystem, recently surpassing one million monthly active developers who use the Streamlit open-source library to build data applications. At Snowflake, we are turning that momentum into the premier enterprise destination for Python-based data applications. Streamlit in Snowflake allows developers to build, share, and deploy governed, interactive applications directly where their data lives.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead this transition from massive open-source momentum to an enterprise business. In this role, you will be the Product Manager of a critical product line, owning the strategy, growth, and P&L for Streamlit in Snowflake. You will bridge the gap between a beloved open-source community and the world’s most sophisticated enterprise customers, ensuring that building a data app in Snowflake is as easy as writing a few lines of Python.

sections.title: AS A SENIOR PM AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:
bullets: Define the Mission: Own the end-to-end strategy for making Streamlit in Snowflake the gold standard for building and running enterprise-grade data applications and AI agents.
Drive Massive Growth: Lead the charge and work with Sales, Marketing and Engineering to grow the Streamlit in Snowflake business.
Own the P&L: Manage the business outcomes for your area, identifying levers for adoption, retention, and monetization across thousands of enterprise accounts.
Architect for AI: Partner with the Cortex AI team to define how LLMs and agentic workflows integrate with Streamlit, enabling users to build using Snowflake’s native AI primitives.

Collaborate Across Boundaries: Act as the primary interface between the Open Source Streamlit team and the Snowflake Enterprise team to ensure a cohesive "one-Streamlit" experience. You will also collaborate with Compute, Networking, Identity and Access teams at Snowflake to define the E2E Streamlit in Snowflake experience.

sections.title: OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE HAS:
bullets: 5+ years of Product Management experience in B2B SaaS, developer platforms, or cloud infrastructure.

A Growth Mindset: A proven track record of taking ambitious products to commercial success at scale.
Dual-Lens UX Focus: High-judgment design skills. You can empathize with a developer using a CLI/SDK and an analyst using a low-code workspace, ensuring the "it just works" experience for both.
Analytical Rigor: You are data-driven and comfortable using metrics and AI-assisted analysis to identify growth gaps and prioritize a roadmap under ambiguity.
High Ownership: You are resilient, low-ego, and thrive in an environment where you are accountable for end-to-end outcomes, good or bad.

bullets: Prior experience with Streamlit (OS or Enterprise) or similar Python app frameworks (Shiny, Dash).
Experience in the AI/ML space , particularly with LLM orchestration or agentic frameworks.
Background in Marketplace or Native App ecosystems .
Prior experience at a high-growth developer-centric company (e.g., Applications Infrastructure or a major Hyperscaler).

ashby:sprig:c4816db4-92af-476c-812b-9efa.summary:
Sprig is the enterprise survey platform, rebuilt around AI agents.

For two decades, companies have relied on Qualtrics, Medallia, and SurveyMonkey to understand their customers and markets. Those platforms were built for a slower era, with manual setup, fragmented workflows, and insights that arrive too late to shape decisions. The gap between how fast businesses move and how fast research can keep up has never been wider.

We're building something different. With Sprig, AI agents design studies, adapt surveys in real time, and turn responses into clear insight. Research, insights, and customer experience teams move from question to evidence in hours instead of weeks, without sacrificing rigor.

sections.title: Abou the role
paras: Exactera helps large multinationals handle complex tax work: transfer pricing, R&D tax credits, indirect tax, and audit defense. We are moving from a software-and-services model to an AI-native platform that does the work itself, with tax practitioners applying judgment where defensibility requires it.

This role owns the product direction for the agentic platform behind that shift: the system that enables AI agents and practitioner tools to run tax analysis on trusted, current data. The data foundation (a lakehouse, external sources, and the contracts that keep them reliable) is the substrate. The product is what agents and practitioners can do with it.

You work directly with the Principal AI Engineer, who owns the AI/ML architecture, and the Principal Data Engineer, who owns the data tier. You own what the platform does, in what order, and why. Because you define how the company’s practitioners and agents use AI, you have to work deeply in these tools yourself.

sections.title: What you'll do
paras:
The six outcomes that define success in the first 18 months.
O1. Own the product strategy and roadmap for the platform.
You own what the platform is for and what it builds next. The roadmap ties to practitioner outcomes rather than feature counts. When priorities compete across engineering, product, and the practice teams, you decide and keep everyone working from the same plan.

O2. Define what compliance-grade means for this platform.
Tax work has to be defensible. You set the product requirements that make the platform’s output trustworthy: where results must be deterministic, what guardrails constrain agent behavior, how tool access is scoped, and what has to be auditable. You decide where human judgment stays in the loop. This is the bar that regulated tax work requires and general AI tooling does not clear.

O3. Own the agentic access surface.
The platform’s main product is the surface AI agents and practitioner tools use to reach data and act on it. You own that surface: the interface, the contracts behind it, and the limits on what agents can do. How this works decides how the whole platform gets used.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: 10+ years in product management, with significant time on technical platform, data, or ML products. You have owned a platform or major product area at Principal-level scope and driven it across teams without positional authority.

Able to set product direction across a modern data platform. You understand Lakehouse and medallion patterns, data contracts, quality, and lineage well enough to decide direction and hold credibility with platform engineers, without needing to build it yourself.
Track record owning AI or ML platform work from an ambiguous problem through to production.
Strong understanding of agentic AI systems and the data access they require: retrieval, tool calling, MCP or equivalent. You can reason about how agents reach data and what should constrain them.

Experience with AI systems where correctness and defensibility matter. You have worked on evaluation, guardrails, or human-in-the-loop design, and you understand why a regulated workflow needs more than a capable model.
You decide what success means for a platform and measure it by practitioner results.
You communicate clearly across engineering, product, and the practice teams. You hold a high bar without leaning on process, and you work well in ambiguity.
You use AI tools as part of how you work day to day, and you share what you learn with the people around you.

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:

Is this identity synthetic? Detect AI-generated and manipulated voice and video.
Is this identity risky? Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.
Is this identity known? Authenticate identities using voice, device, behavioral, and other signals.

Pindrop brings this intelligence together across purpose-built trust engines to help organizations make informed decisions in real time — protecting customers, workforce interactions, and emerging AI-driven interactions.

sections.title: Who We Are

sections.title: What you’ll do

Pindrop is extending its real-time identity trust platform to help enterprises safely service authorized AI agents across communication channels, with verifiable identity, delegated authorization, risk-based controls, and auditable proof of access.

As Senior Product Manager, Agent Identity Management, you will take primary ownership of this emerging product area-from customer validation and product strategy to MVP execution, customer adoption, and commercialization. You will work autonomously with Research, Engineering, Security, Design, and go-to-market teams, making informed technical and commercial trade-offs while building a scalable enterprise offering. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for someone who owns outcomes, not just a feature backlog.
bullets: Own the product vision and roadmap for agent identity management: agent identification, identity verification, authorization signals, and secure servicing decisions, beginning with real-time voice interactions and expanding as customer needs validate.

Lead customer discovery with enterprises, contact center leaders, security and identity teams, and agent ecosystem partners; translate workflows, threat models, and trust requirements into prioritized product opportunities.

Define end-to-end experiences for agent registration or discovery, verified agent claims, delegated user or business authority, risk-based step-up, policy integration, and evidence-rich audit trails - with clear boundaries between Pindrop and enterprise decisions.

Partner with Research, Engineering, and Security to evaluate technical approaches such as cryptographic identity assertions, public-key verification, anti-spoofing, replay protection, and trust signals; make pragmatic tradeoffs across security, usability, interoperability, and time to market.

Drive early-access programs, prototypes, and customer pilots; establish hypotheses, measurable success criteria, and fast feedback loops to validate product-market fit and a repeatable deployment model.
Work with adjacent Pindrop product teams to connect agent identity capabilities with deepfake detection, authentication, risk intelligence, and real-time policy/orchestration workflows.

Shape integrations and ecosystem strategy across enterprise contact center platforms, agent providers, and identity infrastructure. Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success on differentiation, positioning, pricing, packaging, launches, and customer expansion.

Own measurable product and commercial outcomes - including pilot-to-production conversion, adoption, successful authorized-agent servicing, security decision quality, integration time, audit coverage, and revenue potential. Diagnose performance or adoption gaps and drive improvements across teams.

paras: You will own product for the Knowledge Graph and the reporting and analytics experience inside Veeam Data Command Platform (DSPM and AISPM). Actionable dashboards and reporting are how customers see that intelligence, prove their posture to auditors and executives, and decide — and act on — what to fix first.

This is a builder's product role. You will translate a complex graph data model into queries, views, dashboards, and evidence that security, privacy, and governance teams use every day — and you will partner closely with the engineering leader who owns the graph platform and hyperscale lake integrations.
You will set the roadmap, define the metrics that matter, and work AI-first — using agentic tools to prototype, analyze, and ship faster than a traditional PM team.

Drive trending and posture-over-time reporting, including alerting and thresholds, so customers can show risk reduction rather than a single snapshot. Enable downstream and agent consumption: BI integration, warehouse export, and APIs for customers who want the data in their own stack, plus partnering with the AI Agents team to expose graph queries, findings, and posture metrics as MCP tools and resources for customer and internal AI agents

We’ve led the Subscription Economy for more than a decade. Now we’re evolving again by building the definitive platform for quote to cash and helping companies monetize their products and services with an adaptable, AI-ready foundation.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: As a Technical Account Manager (TAM), you’ll be the person our enterprise customers rely on to make Zuora work for their business. You’ll lead solution design across subscription billing, revenue recognition and quote-to-cash. You’ll build AI-assisted proofs of concept (POCs) that show customers what’s possible in days, not months. And you’ll drive the adoption and measurable results that keep customers growing with us.

You’ll own a focused portfolio of enterprise accounts and work as part of a small team, stepping in on teammates’ accounts when your expertise is needed. You’ll partner directly with customers’ finance, IT and executive teams across the US and around the world.

AI has changed what this job can be: routine work like status reports, documentation and first-pass research is increasingly automated, so your time goes to judgment, building, and solving the problems that matter most to the customer.

sections.title: What you’ll own
bullets: Customer outcomes. Own the technical health, adoption and business results of your accounts. Know what success means to each customer in their own terms, such as a faster close, fewer billing errors or a new pricing model launched, and drive toward it.

Solution design and architecture. Lead the design of complex Zuora solutions across billing, revenue recognition and quote-to-cash, including data models, Zuora Workflow, and API integration design with customers’ ERP, CRM and finance systems.
AI-assisted proofs of concept. Use AI tools to build working POCs that demonstrate value and functionality to customers quickly, then turn what works into lasting solutions.
Hands-on problem-solving. Get into the customer’s environment. Use SQL and data analysis to find root causes, validate data and fix problems at the source instead of handing them off.

Closing the loop. When an issue needs Product, Engineering or Support, you stay accountable: you bring in the right people, push for resolution and keep the customer informed. You turn what you learn into product feedback that shapes Zuora’s roadmap.
Customer AI adoption. Help customers adopt AI in their own billing and finance workflows, including how Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and AI agents connect to SaaS platforms like Zuora.

Raising the bar. Share the AI workflows, POCs and patterns you build so the whole team moves faster. Bring what you’ve learned elsewhere, coach teammates on AI and new ways of working, and learn Zuora from them in return.

bullets: First 30 days: Get certified in a Zuora product area.

By 90 days: Own a full portfolio of accounts and drive measurable results for each.

bullets: Experience: A strong track record in SaaS or enterprise software, in roles like implementation, solution consulting, solution architecture or technical account management, where you’ve led complex, customer-facing technical work such as solution design or system integrations.
Fast learner: You’ve picked up new platforms, products or industries quickly and can show how. If you bring the drive, we’ll teach you Zuora and the subscription business.
Builder mindset: You’d rather prototype a solution than write a slide about one, and you can point to things you’ve built.
AI fluency: You use AI tools in your daily work to move faster on prototyping, POCs, data analysis and system architecture, and you can show examples. You understand MCPs and how they apply in SaaS.
Technical depth: Strong SQL, API integration design (REST/SOAP), data modeling and business process design.
Customer focus: You understand how a customer’s business works and tie your work to their results, not just their tickets.
Ownership: You take full accountability for results and close the loop on what you start.

paras: We're looking for a Senior / Principal AI SDLC Engineer to help our financial services clients modernize how software is built, secured, and delivered in an AI-enabled world.

You'll build the secure delivery foundations that allow teams to create, review, test, approve, deploy, and operate software with confidence while meeting governance, security, and audit requirements.

Rather than building customer-facing AI applications, you'll design and evolve the engineering platform that makes enterprise AI development scalable, secure, and repeatable. As a Senior or Principal engineer, you'll influence platform architecture, partner closely with engineering, security, and risk stakeholders, and help shape next-generation software delivery practices for some of Canada's leading financial institutions.

Design and build self-service developer platforms that enable secure, policy-driven software delivery across enterprise environments.
Develop automated delivery pipelines that integrate version control, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, identity, secrets management, artifact repositories, and observability.
Design secure operating models for AI coding agents, including controlled access to repositories, tools, execution environments, permissions, context, approvals, and audit trails.

Strengthen the software supply chain through automated security practices including SAST, SCA, secrets detection, SBOM generation, artifact signing, provenance, dependency governance, and controlled promotion.
Automate governance requirements such as separation of duties, approvals, traceability, retention, evidence collection, and compliance reporting without slowing delivery.

Build risk-based deployment strategies including progressive delivery, release approvals, rollback capabilities, and automated release evidence for both deterministic and AI-assisted development workflows.

lever:vida:8aa51262-bfda-4c94-989a-bb76b.summary:
Most product managers build what members, providers, or clients see. This role builds the systems that make the whole company run.

Behind every member interaction at Vida is a chain of systems: eligibility data, our member admin tools, Zendesk, Braze, our EHR, pharmacy and device vendors, and a data warehouse. Today, too many of those links are held together by spreadsheets, manual steps, and a few people who know where everything lives. When a link breaks, a member waits, a support agent files a ticket, and an engineer goes digging.

You'll own that layer. You'll learn how our member support, clinical operations, and device operations teams actually work, map how our tools talk (or don't) to each other, and set the vision and roadmap for how they should. You'll partner with a dedicated engineer, our Zendesk lead, and the operations leaders who depend on these systems every day.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Own the vision and roadmap for operations systems. Turn a long list of stakeholder requests into a clear point of view on what our internal systems should do, and a sequenced plan to get there.
Shadow support agents and ops teams. Understand what they do, which tools they use, where time is lost, and what would move time-to-first-touch, time-to-resolution and cost-to-serve.

Design how systems connect. Read vendor API docs (Zendesk, Braze, our EHR, fulfillment partners), understand our internal data models, define integrations, data flows, and automations that work reliably at scale.
Replace manual work with durable systems. Find processes that run on spreadsheets, scheduled refreshes, and human memory, especially where a failure delays care, and design their replacements.
Give operations teams visibility. Shape internal tools that let a support agent open a member record and see what happened, in what order, and why, without filing an engineering ticket.
Be a peer to operations leaders, not a ticket-taker. Push back, reframe requests into problems, and bring back plans that serve the whole business.
Reverse-engineer what's already there. Some of our systems were built by people who've moved on. You'll piece together how they work from code, docs, data, and conversations.
Additional responsibilities as needed.

sections.title: Qualifications:
bullets: Bachelor's degree at a minimum.
7+ years in product management, with meaningful time on internal, operations, or business systems (support ops, rev ops, marketing ops, clinical or fulfillment ops, business technology).
Hands-on experience designing integrations between third-party platforms such as Zendesk, Salesforce, Braze, HubSpot or Twilio, and internal systems.
Fluency reading API documentation and reasoning about data flows: webhooks, JSON payloads, event triggers, sync vs. async, failure and retry.

Comfortable in technical environments: you can read code in Python or JavaScript, find your way around GitHub, and understand the basics of AWS or Google Cloud and SQL. You don't need to write production code.
A track record of turning messy, manual processes into scalable systems, with outcomes you can measure.
The judgment to see how data flows, workflows, and automations should fit together, not just one at a time.
Strong stakeholder skills with senior operations leaders, including saying no and proposing a better path.
